summary: Two demonstrated defects in core derivations: D.1 halves the constructed output; Lemma31 lacks weighted-tail control and is false at stated generality. Main theorem not claimed false. Strict separation comparisons need restricted regimes.

problems.title: Output representation is scaled by one half
assumptions: v uniform ±1; b uniform[-1,1]; shifted windows length2A contained in[-1,1]
Gaussian inputs; unit beta; normalized polynomial link
problems.check: Window probability A, sign probability1/2, prefactor1/(2A) gives1/4 each conditional expectation, while next display uses1/2. With pi'=2v/alpha the exact integral equalsZ/2.
problems.result: Error |Z|/2 does not vanish in probability.
problems.counterevidence: Existence/rate theorem may survive a constant-factor repair; experimental weights not evaluated.
problems.impact: Invalid construction feeds Lemma24 and main optimization/inference guarantee.

correction.verification: Exact density and ReLU integral identity; asymptotic norm orders unchanged
correction.scope: Local construction only; full theorem repair not certified

problems.title: Weighted Gaussian concentration lemma omits tail moment
problems.location: PDF p31 Lemma31; p32 Cor32; pp20-25 Lemmas19-21
problems.claim: High-probability |z_i|<=C alone implies concentration around E[zX] at Otilde(Csqrt(d/N)).
assumptions: iid weights allowed to depend on Xi
All expectations finite; exceptional event superpolynomially rare
problems.check: E[zX]=(2pi)^-1/2 e1, while all weighted samples vanish with probability>=1-d² GaussianTail(d). Claimed bound decays Otilde(d^-1/2), actual error is constant.
problems.result: Lemma false; proof drops z from weighted tail expectation.
problems.counterevidence: Lemma18 provides actual weighted-moment technique applicable to Lemma19; complete matrix-tail control at Lemma21 not independently verified.
problems.impact: False concentration premise used in core attention optimization chain; no claim that main theorem or experiments are false.

correction.statement: Retain b_d=||E[zX1{|z|>C}]|| in concentration inequality; bound it separately for each application.
correction.verification: Analytic triangle inequality and bounded-weight Gaussian concentration; local lemma correction supported

problems.title: Low-degree strict rate advantage does not follow
problems.claim: ge<=degree ensures superiority of displayed inference rate in all regimes.
assumptions: Compare stated sufficient exponent with paper's own comparator exponents
problems.check: Theorem exponent3 exceeds kernel2 and CSQ1; He3 exponent1.5 equalsCSQ1.5.
problems.result: Strict separation needs degree>1.5ge or ie>3ge.
problems.counterevidence: High-degree existential separation remains; an upper bound is not an algorithmic lower bound.
problems.impact: Overbroad comparison, not refutation of explicit sufficient-rate theorem.

correction.statement: Restrict comparisons to strict exponent inequalities.
